title: Japan Sees Rise in Southeast Asian Residents
paragraphs: Japan's foreign population is growing, but it's still much smaller than in other G7 countries — a group that also includes Canada, France, Germany, Italy, the UK and the US.

According to the latest census, foreign nationals made up 3% of Japan's population in 2025. In every other G7 country, the figure is above 10%, according to data from the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
And the countries people are coming from are changing. Much of Japan's recent growth has come from Southeast Asia, particularly Vietnam, Indonesia and Myanmar.

For example, the number of Indonesian nationals living in Japan has quadrupled since 2020, reaching more than 226,000 in 2025. The population from Myanmar has grown even faster, increasing by almost six times to over 163,000.
But Vietnam has the largest population in Japan of any Southeast Asian country.
Over five years, Japan's Vietnamese population grew by 59% to more than 609,000. That means Vietnamese nationals now make up almost 16% of Japan's foreign population.
In fact, people from Vietnam have overtaken Koreans to become the country's second-largest foreign group, behind only people from China.
Researcher Ayumi Minamida also told Nikkei Asia that more Vietnamese people are getting visas of a type for engineers, specialists in humanities and providers of international services.
Meanwhile, the Korean population in Japan is moving in the opposite direction.
The number of Korean nationals has fallen by 8% since 2020 to around 398,000. And more than 30% are now aged 65 or older, a higher proportion than in Japan's population as a whole.
Chinese nationals are still the largest foreign group in Japan, with more than 923,000 people, up 18% since 2020.

So Japan's foreign population isn't just getting bigger — the countries people are coming from are changing too, with more Vietnamese nationals now living in Japan than Koreans, and Southeast Asian populations growing rapidly.
